newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan foreign minister to visit Britain and France.
newsitem.headline: Japan foreign minister to visit Britain and France.

text.p: Japanese Foreign Minister Yukihiko Ikeda will visit Britain and France after a planned three-day trip to Russia this week, the Foreign Ministry announced on Wednesday.
Ikeda is scheduled to leave Tokyo on Thursday for Moscow, where he will hold talks on bilateral and international issues with President Boris Yeltsin and Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov.

The talks are aimed at preparing for an exchange of visits of prime ministers before the end of the year and next month's Denver summit of the Group of Seven (G7) major industrialised countries, which Russia will attend for the first time as a full member, the Foreign Ministry said.

In an apparent warming of bilateral ties, Russian Defence Minister Igor Rodionov on Sunday concluded a visit to Japan in which he promised troop cuts and expanded defence exchanges with Tokyo and gave Moscow's blessing to closer U.S.-Japan military ties.

Ikeda will spend the weekend in London, where he will hold talks with new Foreign Secretary Robin Cook, then travel to Paris, where he will attend a ministerial meeting of the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD).
Ikeda is scheduled to hold talks with South Korean Foreign Minister Yoo Chong-ha and French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette in Paris before returning to Japan on May 29.
